articles.title: “You feel no one cares about you in Akron”: LeBron James opens up on how growing up in Akron shaped him as he changes countless lives there
articles.summary: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ star player, has kept his focus on the last season in court as he is all set to retire after the upcoming
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ star player, has kept his focus on the last season in court as he is all set to retire after the upcoming season. While LeBron James gears up to play for the Philadelphia 76ers, he has remained passionate about Akron. Amid this, LeBron James’ comments on his roots in Akron have moved many.LeBron James reflects on his love and dedication for Akron and growing up there in a middle class homeIn an interview with the Los Angeles Times’ Dan Woike, the four time NBA champion, LeBron James opened up about his love for Akron as he said, “People always say, ‘You’re going back home.’ But I tell people all the time, ‘I’m not from Cleveland.’”The star player added, “There’s no disrespect to Cleveland. But, when you’re from Akron, you’re not from Cleveland,” James told Woike. “This is where I’m from.”LeBron James also reflected on the childhood he has had in Akron as he said, “When you grow up in Akron, Ohio, you already feel like no one cares about you too much,” he said. “And the only people that really care about you are the ones from that town.”He added, “When you are in certain community centers, in certain gyms, you look for inspiration—people who came before you, people who were already there.”LeBron James has continuously worked towards Akron’s developments and changed thousands of lives thereIn the last two decades, as and when LeBron James’ wealth grew after being drafted in the league, he remained loyal to his hometown and has continued to donate.Apart from his foundations, LeBron James has also been there for his alma mater, St. Vincent–St. Mary High School, as he funded a $1 million renovation for the school’s gym.While St. Vincent–St. Mary basketball has continued to add new talents, LeBron James reflected on it as he said, “It means you set the path along the way while you’re doing it for the next generation. It was our whole thing while we were there…”The four time NBA champion added, “It started with Maverick [Carter] and Derrick and Darren Tarver, guys who were there already. And we came in and wanted to pave the way for the next generation. We wanted St. Vincent–St. Mary to be a school that didn’t just have one-offs. They’re still doing it.”Set up in 2004, the LeBron James' Family Foundation have consciously worked on helping to develop the communities in Akron as the NBA legend has also set up a number of schools there for children belonging to underprivileged and unstable backgrounds.In the last few months, LeBron James has also partnered with Mercedes Maybach and PGA Tour to help in development.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Kawhi Leonard sat out Raptors’ preseason game as Heat dominated in Quebec City
articles.summary: Miami Heat secured a stunning and dominating win in Quebec City on Saturday, and Kawhi Leonard never made it onto the floor in the Raptors' preseason
articles.body: Miami Heat secured a stunning and dominating win in Quebec City on Saturday, and Kawhi Leonard never made it onto the floor in the Raptors' preseason opener. Raptors coach Darko Rajakovic had hinted at the outcome a day earlier, then confirmed it before tipoff at Videotron Centre. Miami led 120-101 with about two minutes left.Toronto describes the absence as a planned ramp-up after a long summer on hold, and the schedule stretches well past one night. Even the Oct. 10 game against the Clippers in Vancouver looks like a long shot.Why Kawhi Leonard did not play for the Raptors against the Heat in Quebec CityKawhi Leonard sat out because the Raptors are rebuilding his conditioning after a long summer on hold, and the team says no new injury is involved. Rajakovic told reporters before tipoff that Leonard would not face the Heat at Videotron Centre. He also said Leonard likely misses the Oct. 10 game in Vancouver. “The Raptors have been taking it slow with the oft-injured Leonard in camp, a very light head-to-head drill between the coach and the superstar after Friday's practice notwithstanding. He has yet to participate in full-contact drills," according to The Canadian Press.Leonard moved from the Clippers to Toronto in June, but the deal stalled for most of the summer while the NBA examined salary-cap circumvention involving the player and the Clippers. Rajakovic ties the long layoff directly to that pause.Leonard helped Toronto win its first NBA championship in 2019. Last season with the Clippers produced 27.9 points and 3.6 assists per game over 65 appearances, plus a spot on the All-NBA second team.The 35-year-old forward has worked through drills at practice but has not joined full-contact sessions. Leonard also skipped the intrasquad scrimmage, and the Raptors keep calling the whole process reconditioning.Rajakovic offered a lighter moment after Friday's practice, joking that Leonard had earned a game against the Heat by winning a light one-on-one. The drill was light, and the plan stayed as it was. The coach was more serious about the bigger picture, calling the situation "a day-to-day thing with Kawhi."How the Heat pulled away and what comes next for Kawhi LeonardWithout Leonard, Toronto spent most of the night chasing. Miami dropped 41 points on the Raptors in the opening quarter and carried an 18-point lead into the second. The second quarter was closer, 35-32 in Miami's favor, though the damage was done by then. By halftime, the Heat were up 76-55.The Raptors won the third quarter 25-19, trimming the gap to 15 heading into the fourth. Miami had added 25 more by the time the clock showed 2:11, with the score at 120-101. Both teams are 0-0, so the score only reflects the preseason. Finally, the Heat secured 129-105 win.TSN's Josh Lewenberg reported that Leonard is expected to miss the first two preseason games, a stretch that covers the Oct. 10 meeting with the Clippers in Vancouver.Toronto enters the 2026-27 season with real expectations and has been open about prioritizing a gradual buildup for Leonard. If the plan holds, Leonard still has three preseason chances to play before the regular season starts.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 6-foot-9 Luka Doncic’s Lakers teammate makes romantic move with longtime girlfriend at Bruno Mars Concert
articles.summary: Ziaire Williams went to SoFi Stadium on Friday night for a Bruno Mars show, but the Lakers wing had a bigger plan than singing along.
articles.body: Ziaire Williams went to SoFi Stadium on Friday night for a Bruno Mars show, but the Lakers wing had a bigger plan than singing along. Mars and the stadium crew both appeared to be in on it.The song was "Marry You," and Williams used it to propose to his girlfriend while cameras rolled. The video board carried the moment to the stadium, and fans soon passed the clip around online. The Lakers have not even opened the preseason yet, which makes it the first big headline of their new season.Ziaire Williams proposes to girlfriend at Bruno Mars concertZiaire Williams picked a stadium concert for a question that usually gets asked in private. The proposal came on Friday night at SoFi Stadium, right as Bruno Mars performed "Marry You." Mars and the stadium staff appeared to know the surprise was coming. Cameras caught the moment, and the video board put it in front of the crowd so everyone could celebrate with the couple.The song choice did half the work. Few tracks announce the question as clearly as "Marry You," and the crowd had an easy cue to cheer.SoFi Stadium posted its own reaction on X. "It really was a beautiful night 🥹💍," the venue wrote, tagging Mars. Fan video spread as well. A post from @MrBuckBuckNBA, sharing a clip from @Kjblazin, read:“Ziaire Williams just proposed to his girlfriend at the Bruno mars concert. Way to start your journey with the Lakers.”The night also fits a busy summer for Williams. He joined the Lakers a few months ago, a move that brought the 25-year-old home and set up a reunion with high school teammate Bronny James.Williams turns attention to Lakers camp and a starting roleThe calendar did not leave much room for a victory lap. The Lakers went back to the practice court on Saturday and open a five-game preseason slate on Monday, on the road against the Sacramento Kings. Williams is one of the players competing for a starting spot, so this camp carries real weight for the wing.Memphis drafted Williams, and Brooklyn gave the wing the last two seasons. At Lakers media day, Williams talked about wanting to be in a winning environment. "I play to win, right?" Williams said. The mindset came from Williams' father, who taught the value of competing whatever the stat sheet says.The standard in Los Angeles is a championship, Williams said of Luka Doncic's team, and the wing is fully on board with that goal. Winning at home, with family and friends in the building, carries extra meaning.A bigger role could follow. Williams could grow into one of the Lakers' best wing defenders, provided the offense keeps improving.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation makes major impact as it raises $15 million for youth programs ahead of the new season
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have done their best to help the community they grew up in Oakland.
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have done their best to help the community they grew up in Oakland. While both of them have their own professional lives, they have remained committed to their cause. Amid this, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, has made an update about their fundraising.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, makes an update about the funds they have been able to raiseA few days ago, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, took to their social media to make a post that read as, “50 years of the Memorial Tournament, and Eat. Learn. Play. got to be part of the celebration! Since 2022, @memorialgolf has raised over $15 million for youth programs in Oakland and Columbus. We’re proud to be a beneficiary of this storied event. Highlight of the week: co-hosting a golf and football clinic for the Golden Cubs, current and former patients of @nationwidekids. @ohiostatefb showed up to surprise them, and of course the Memorial’s signature milkshakes made an appearance.”The post added, “None of this happens without @Workday. Since 2019, their partnership with @eatlearnplay has helped raise $12 million for our work in Oakland — through The Memorial, at our annual Workday Charity Classic, and every day in between. Thank you, Workday, for showing up for our kids all year long.”While the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry keeps himself busy with the season in the league, he has continued to look for different ways to raise funds for the foundation, Eat, Learn & Play.Back in November last year, as Stephen Curry ended his contract with Under Armour, he wore sneakers of different brands to the court.Later, all the sneakers he wore during this time were auctioned off to raise funds for their foundation.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation helps children to eat well, study more and even participate in sportsIn the last few years, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, has constantly worked towards helping to improve lives of children in their hometown who belong to underprivileged backgrounds.The foundation was initially set up to help more and more children in Oakland to have access to education and quality meals which many were missing out on as families struggled with poverty.Seven years down the line, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, has changed thousands of lives across Oakland.While quality education and nutritious meals have been given top priority, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, has also been actively trying to inculcate sports as a habit among children in Oakland.The foundation continues to build playgrounds across Oakland to help more and more families.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “It all started with a kid from Akron”: LeBron James’ foundation celebrates major achievement as I PROMISE program serves 2500 students
articles.summary: LeBron James, the four time NBA champion, has always been public about the difficulties he faced in his life while growing up in Akron as he was raised by
articles.body: LeBron James, the four time NBA champion, has always been public about the difficulties he faced in his life while growing up in Akron as he was raised by his mother alone. While LeBron James is easily one of the most popular players in the world today, his foundation, the LeBron James Family Foundation, has shared an update about helping 2500 students across Akron.LeBron James’ foundation makes a major impact on lives of 2,500 students in Akron ahead of the new seasonA few days ago, the LeBron James Family Foundation took to social media to make a post that read as, “It all started with a kid from Akron and a bike… 🚲 When @kingjames was growing up in Akron, those two wheels gave him the freedom and mobility needed to get to the park, the rec center to shoot hoops, and places where he could be with his community.”The post added, “Throughout his journey, those two wheels have continued to represent the opportunities, accessibility, and the feeling of freedom only a bike can provide. For the @ljfamfoundation, that was literally captured in the bike-a-thon, a notable event that did good for a day, which has evolved into the I Promise program now serving over 2,500 students with all the resources they need to access their dreams.”The LeBron James Family Foundation’s social media post continued, “That history is a huge part of why you’ll see so many wheels all throughout Buckets. We wanted to pay homage to our humble beginnings as a Foundation and the journey that helped get us here, because we promise to never forget where we came from.”Despite his busy life, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon LeBron James has been a strong pillar of strength and community to the Akron community he grew up in.LeBron James has often spoken about the issues he faced as his mother raised him in Akron before he made it big in his lifeLeBron James and his wife, Savannah James, have remained united when it comes to being there for the children of Akron.Coming from a similar background, both LeBron James and his wife, Savannah James, have always been understanding of the issues the children in Akron have been facing.In many of his interviews, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon LeBron James has spoken about how growing up in Akron was difficult due to the middle class background he came from.Despite the problems he faced in his childhood, the NBA icon LeBron James pushed through and is a popular billionaire today.With all the money he has earned, LeBron James has been passionate about using it to help people and communities in Akron.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dream's defensive showcase, led by Angel Reese, stymies Liberty in Game 1 of WNBA semifinals: '[DPOY] is in Atlanta for a reason'
articles.summary: Angel Reese was named Defensive Player of the Year this week, and Sunday's performance in Game 1 showed exactly why.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — Angel Reese keeps her vision board to herself and checks off items as the season progresses. She knocked off Defensive Player of the Year this month , one of the items listed at the bottom as one of her individual aspirations, and accepted the trophy in front of the home fans on Sunday.

When she did, she added a task to a to-do list: she intends to engrave it with the names of Atlanta Dream teammates Jordin Canada and Rhyne Howard. She's been saying for weeks now that any of the three league leaders in steals were worthy of the award.

Few would argue with that in the aftermath of a 92-82 win over the No. 8 New York Liberty in Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals on Sunday. No one who watched the third-quarter suffocation of two former MVPs and an all-WNBA guard, specifically, would dissent.

"It goes to show," Angel Reese told a group of reporters post-game. "Defensive Player of the Year is in Atlanta for a reason."

The Dream snatched balls out of bellies and smacked them out of the air. In the second quarter, Reese denied Sabrina Ionescu at the rim and delivered a staredown to an amped courtside crowd. In one third-quarter sequence, Canada played swiper three times in a row. Collectively, they smothered a team that still starts four players from their 2024 championship team.

The Liberty couldn't sniff a whiff of the paint if it were a perfume store. Atlanta locked them out, forcing drivers wide and shots off target. The Dream fully shut the door in a deafening third quarter that should rattle the thought of a Liberty Finals.

New York led 40-37 at the half. It was a grind of a game, but one they could break through. They were shooting better (43.8%) than the Dream (34.3%) and began to find their groove offensively, allowing Breanna Stewart to pull up in the mid-range and Pauline Astier to drive.

DeWanna Bonner, a rare late-season acquisition who's already one of the best midseason signings of the decade, lit into her young, inexperienced roster. Reese, Howard and Allisha Gray, who sustained a hand injury and only played 10:47, are playing in their first semifinals. Bonner notched postseason game No. 101 on Sunday. She declined to divulge exactly what she said.

Canada, who won two titles with Stewart and Sue Bird in Seattle in her first and third seasons, shared the basics. They needed a second-half surge that started in the first three minutes of the quarter.

"It started defensively with our energy," Canada said. "We were able to get stops and get out in transition, which is what we do best, and from there we were able to separate a little bit and finish off."

It was a return to the unfancy, yet no less skilled, bread and butter that carried them here. They turned the Liberty over nine times in the frame for 16 points, more than the Liberty's 15 points as a team. New York shot 42.9% from the perimeter with three 3s, but 1 of 7 from inside the arc (14%). Jones and Stewart, with their inside presence, combined to shoot 1 of 4. The Dream pounded the paint (18-2), won in transition (11-0) and off second chances (5-0).

Canada, the veteran point guard, came back from early foul trouble — "I might have been a little bit too handsy," she admitted — finished the game with a team-high five steals, 25 points and even a block. Reese had four steals and three blocks, along with 17 points, 7 rebounds, 2 assists and 4 turnovers. Howard scored 16 with a team-high eight assists. Bonner had 23 points, going 10 of 18 and 3 of 6 from 3. Each had one steal, as six of nine players who saw the court stole it at least once.

One-third of Atlanta's total offense came from points off turnovers. They turned the Liberty over 21 times — nearly identical to the 20 they had in two of their three regular-season games against Atlanta — for 32 points. It tied the WNBA postseason record for points off turnovers.

"We'll go back and watch the film and just understand those points off turnovers really mattered, especially on a team that feeds off of it," Ionescu said.

An understatement of the century. Ionescu, Stewart and first-year head coach Chris DeMarco all said afterward they knew Atlanta's favorite meal. They were aware that live-ball turnovers would be key. It was the question posed to them all week leading into their semifinal appearance as a No. 8 seed, the first to do so in league history. Stewart noted the Dream did this exact same thing two weeks ago in the regular season.

Left unsaid: They couldn't do anything about it.

"We need to be better," Stewart said. "We need to be more prepared and expect that."

Atlanta successfully set the semifinals' tone in the franchise's first appearance since 2018. The Dream, which came into the league as a 2008 expansion team, has never won a championship despite reaching the Finals three times in four years between 2010 and 2013. They finished the regular season as one of the league's best defensive units, limiting the fastbreak and second-chance points. They averaged a league-high 9.1 steals per game.

They've upped it in the playoffs. Rarely could New York beat them back on offense, forcing the Liberty to fight for every inch. Not even Stewart, the three-time WNBA champion too often dragging this Liberty team to success, could save them with a late flurry. A steal-and-score pulled the Liberty to within five with 2:50 to play. It was the third time in 2:30 of game time they pulled as close. Atlanta led by as many as 16.

On her way back down the court's sideline, Reese yelled and motioned "settle down" with a purpose. She told head coach Karl Smesko to call a timeout. He obliged.

In red carpet-worthy street clothes, her Defensive Player of the Year trophy safe in the bowels of State Farm Arena, Reese said she felt the team was getting too high and needed to regroup.

"We wanted to make sure we were better than that, because this is the playoffs," Reese said. "Anybody can come back, and especially in this environment. If this was in New York, I mean, it could have went another way, especially with their crowd into it."

The three-game series made Reese nervous. Anything can happen in those, she said. A five-game series gives more of a runway, which DeMarco said he will take as the Liberty make those adjustments for Game 2 on Wednesday.

"I don't want to dictate and rely on five games," Reese said. "I want to be able to win, win, win, win, win and move onto the next round. That's kind of how the mindset has been."

To reach the playoffs for the first time in her three-year career was technically on her goal sheet. But she said she knew she would reach it playing for the Dream, the team that traded for her on the dawn of an abbreviated offseason window. Clinching the semifinals proved the franchise could get over the hump after Howard, Gray and Canada lost in the first round a year ago.

At the top of the vision board are team goals, led by the one she said earlier on Sunday would mean more than DPOY: a WNBA championship. They're one defensive showcase closer to it.

articles.title: LA Clippers injury update: 6-foot-5 star hit with concerning news in preseason opener vs Golden State Warriors
articles.summary: Max Strus was five minutes into his Clippers debut when a routine cut turned ugly.
articles.body: Max Strus was five minutes into his Clippers debut when a routine cut turned ugly. The 6-foot-5 forward came off a screen, caught a pass from Darius Garland, and hopped away from the play on one leg. Coach Ty Lue called a timeout. Strus walked to the locker room and never came back to the preseason opener against the Golden State Warriors.Reports point to a right foot problem, and the Clippers have not offered a diagnosis. Brandon Ingram is already sidelined for the start of the season, and opening night is about three weeks away.Max Strus injury update: What happened in the Clippers' preseason openerMax Strus went down on Sunday night with a little over seven minutes left in the first quarter. The play itself looked ordinary. Strus ran off a screen with Stephen Curry chasing him, took the pass from Garland on the wing, and seemed to tweak something right after the catch. He hopped on the left foot to get away from the action. No other player was close enough to blame, so this looks like a non-contact injury.Lue stopped the game, and Strus went to see the team doctors. Clippers reporter Joey Linn relayed that the forward would not return with a right foot injury. Other accounts of the play call it a right ankle issue, which means the exact problem is still unclear.Strus played five minutes, grabbed one rebound, and missed the lone shot he took. Rookie Keaton Wagler picked up most of the minutes left behind, while Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr. and Cam Christie also saw larger roles.Why the Strus injury could hurt the Clippers' seasonStrus was likely headed for a first-half cap anyway, since teams usually go easy in preseason. That does not explain the limp. Foot trouble has followed him before. Last season with the Cleveland Cavaliers, Strus missed the first 67 games while recovering from a fractured left foot and finished with only 12 appearances. In those games, he averaged 11.2 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.0 assists, shooting 44.3 percent from the field and 40.2 percent from three.There is one encouraging detail. This time the right foot is involved, so it does not appear to be a flare-up of the old break. Strus arrived in August through a five-team trade centered on Peyton Watson, which makes this a first look at the fit that got cut short.The roster has little cushion. Ingram came over from the Toronto Raptors in the Kawhi Leonard trade, and nobody has a return date for him. The Leonard penalty also cost the Clippers their first-round picks, so a losing year would sting twice. A crowded Western Conference does not leave much room to stumble.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nikola Jokić dazzles with behind-the-back pass down the baseline that you have to see to believe
articles.summary: Nikola Jokić is already doing Nikola Jokić things.
articles.body:
Nikola Jokić is already doing Nikola Jokić things.

The do-everything three-time MVP center was in action for the Denver Nuggets for a preseason game against the Utah Jazz Sunday night. Playing up the road from Denver on the University of Colorado's campus, Jokić uncorked this beauty for the Boulder home crowd.

Being able to imagine that pass to begin with is remarkable. There's probably nobody else in the NBA who would even think about it, much less consider executing it. And then Jokić did exactly just that.

He threw a no-look, behind the-back pass from one 3-point corner to the other directly down the baseline, bypassing three Jazz defenders in the process. Cam Johnson then made good on the sorcery, hoisting a catch-and-shoot 3-pointer that sank through the net.

Jokić, meanwhile, was already headed back on defense while Johnson's shot was in the air, correctly confident in the play's success.

It was a thing of basketball beauty from a meaningless basketball game that counts for nothing. But thankfully, it was caught on camera to inspire awe among the lovers of the game.

And soon enough, those passes will count. The Nuggets open their season in an Oct. 22 matchup against the Oklahoma City Thunder that will certainly matter.

articles.title: King Gibson Commits to Will Wade's LSU, Everything to Know About 5-Star Guard Recruit
articles.summary: Will Wade and LSU basketball landed a major recruit on Sunday.
articles.body:
Will Wade and LSU basketball landed a major recruit on Sunday.

Per ESPN's Jeff Borzello, class of 2027 5-star guard King Gibson announced his commitment to the Tigers.

NFL investigating 2 referees for separate viral exchanges

Gibson is considered by 247Sports' composite rankings to be the No. 15 player in the class of 2027 and the No. 3 combo guard in the country. Gibson holds offers from countless schools, with Baylor, Louisville, Arkansas and Providence joining LSU as his top choices.

He visited all five programs over the past few months before ultimately landing on the Tigers.

Gibson is originally from Greensboro, North Carolina, but is gearing up for his second season at SPIRE Academy, a nationally coveted basketball program in Ohio.

Gibson marks the second commitment for LSU out of the class of 2027. He joins Ahmad Hudson, a 5-star power forward who is ranked as the No. 19 player in his class.

To say that LSU basketball is a team in need of a spark would be an understatement. The Tigers have not made the NCAA tournament since the final season of Wade's first tenure in 2022.

With Matt McMahon leading the way over the past four years, the Tigers have finished better than .500 just one time. They went 15-17 overall and 3-15 in conference play, finishing second-to-last in the SEC.

LSU brought Wade back this spring and is hoping his second stint with the team will lead to the success the school has been after for years. After landing a top recruit on Sunday, it's safe to say Wade is building a competitive program.

articles.title: “I think we need another big”: Anthony Davis reveals how his genuine ask for roster change led to NBA shocker trade involving Luka Doncic in 2025
articles.summary: Anthony Davis got up to roughly 268 pounds in his last year with the Lakers, and the extra weight explains the request Davis made for another big man.
articles.body: Anthony Davis got up to roughly 268 pounds in his last year with the Lakers, and the extra weight explains the request Davis made for another big man. The NBA champion told the Wizards' Numbers on the Board podcast that the added pounds left him feeling "heavy."Playing center against Joel Embiid and Nikola Jokic at that size wore Davis down, and cutting weight midseason did not fix it. The Lakers never added a second big. Instead, they traded Davis to Dallas for Luka Doncic.Why Anthony Davis asked the Lakers for another big manThe ask came two weeks before the 2025 trade deadline. Anthony Davis told ESPN's Shams Charania that the Lakers needed a center to become real title contenders. The big man also wanted to go back to playing the four, the spot where the game fits best. "I think we need another big," Davis said.On the Wizards' Numbers on the Board podcast, Davis explained that usually played at 250 or 255 pounds. In his last year in Los Angeles, the scale climbed to 265 and maybe 268.The strength work was meant to prepare Davis for life at center, where natural centers like Joel Embiid and Nikola Jokic were beating Davis up night after night. Davis did not feel right in that body. "Bro, I can't play like this. I feel heavy," Davis said.Davis tried to cut weight during the season, but dropping pounds while still guarding centers every night was tough. He later sent a request to the front office. Nothing came of it. The Lakers did chase center Mark Williams from the Charlotte Hornets, but the trade was rescinded.The big request turned to a NBA shocker tradeThe Lakers answered with a trade nobody saw coming. Davis, Max Christie and a 2029 first-round pick went to the Mavericks for Doncic, Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris. ESPN's Charania posted the deal, which also pulled in Utah. Jalen Hood-Schifino went to the Jazz to balance the money. Plenty of fans still call it the most shocking trade in NBA history.The weight problem traveled to Dallas. In the fall of 2025, Davis reported to Mavericks camp at 268 pounds, and fans got nervous. Further, an early calf strain limited him. Once the weight came off, the usual two-way game returned. In December, Davis put up 32 points and 13 rebounds against Jokic and the Nuggets.Davis has since been traded again, this time to Washington. The Wizards have Alex Sarr, Deandre Ayton, and Tristan Vukcevic, all able to play center, so the Wizards forward gets the starting power forward job he asked for in 2025. Playing alongside another big man, Davis said, is "a different, you know, ball game for me."This year, it will be interesting to see Davis’ play in the Wizards.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Tobias Harris' injury update from San Antonio came with no timetable attached.
articles.body: Tobias Harris' injury update from San Antonio came with no timetable attached. Coach Mitch Johnson told reporters Sunday that the Spurs will let a left calf strain heal at its own pace, even with the season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Oct. 20 getting close.San Antonio signed Harris this offseason to share the frontcourt with Victor Wembanyama, and his first camp has been interrupted by a strain with no firm return date. The $31 million forward sat out the weekend scrimmage and will be checked again once the preseason wraps up.Tobias Harris injury update: Spurs coach says there is no rush on the calf strainTobias Harris, 34, strained a left calf muscle in training camp, and the Spurs made the news public Sunday. The team lists Harris as questionable for the Oct. 20 opener and says a fresh evaluation will come after the preseason. Roughly two weeks separate the announcement from opening night.The Spurs announced the strain, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reported that Harris would not suit up for the scrimmage, and Johnson addressed it afterward at Frost Bank Center, "We won't rush him at all."The coach added that the staff sees no cause for alarm at this level of seriousness, though he stopped short of rating the strain. Asked about the opener, Johnson said Harris' availability is very much in doubt and the team will not push him toward that game. San Antonio has not given a return date or a number of weeks, so the next real update comes when Harris is reevaluated after the preseason, which opens Oct. 8 at home against the Atlanta Hawks and runs five games.How the Spurs lineup could look without himThe 6-foot-8 forward is not an easy piece to replace. Harris spent the past two seasons in Detroit, and last year the Pistons won 60 games and finished first in the East while Harris averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 63 appearances. Harris also shot 46.9% from the field and 36.8% from three in 27.7 minutes a night.San Antonio saw a big offseason pickup in those numbers. The idea was to add veteran presence and versatility to a team coming off a historic run to the 2026 NBA Finals. Harris was projected as the main frontcourt partner for Wembanyama, and the two-year, $31 million contract makes this more than a depth issue. Harris lists at small forward and power forward, so the injury touches more than one spot in the rotation.Without Harris, the Spurs will likely turn to the group that carried them last year, including Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie, with Dylan Harper coming off the bench. articles.title: Raquel Carrera no pudo ayudar a las Liberty en su derrota ante las Dream en las semifinales de la WNBA
articles.standfirst: as Valkyries doblegan a las Aces y se adelantan 1-0 en las semifinales de la WNBA
articles.summary: as Valkyries doblegan a las Aces y se adelantan 1-0 en las semifinales de la WNBA
articles.body: Las Golden State Valkyries doblegaron a Las Vegas Aces en el primer partido de las semifinales de la WNBA, jugadas al mejor de siete encuentros, al imponerse en casa por 71-60. Gabby Williams lideró la victoria con un gran doble doble de 25 puntos y 11 rebotes, con cinco de once desde el arco, apoyada por los once puntos de Kaitlyn Chen. Las Aces, que nunca había metido menos de 89 puntos en esta postemporada, tuvieron una noche complicada con el tiro. A'ja Wilson fue su líder anotadora con 24 puntos, Chelsea Gray metió 16 y Jackie Young no pasó de los once. El segundo partido de la serie se jugará el miércoles en San Francisco. En la otra semifinal, las Atlanta Dream tomaron ventaja gracias a un 92-82 en casa contra las New York Liberty. Las Dream fueron lideradas por 25 puntos de Jordin Canada y por 23 de DeWanna Bonner, mientras que Angel Reese contribuyó con 17 puntos y 7 rebotes. Las Liberty, que dieron la sorpresa en la primera ronda al eliminar a las Minnesota Lynx, pagaron un tercer cuarto perdido 32-15. Su máxima anotadora fue Sabrina Ionescu, con 27 puntos, y Breanna Stewart aportó 19 puntos. La española Raquel Carrera no jugó con las Liberty. Las Finales de la WNBA se disputarán a partir del 17 de octubre al mejor de 7 partidos.

articles.title: Payton Pritchard Could be Main Factor in Boston Celtics Success This Season
articles.summary: The sixth-year point guard will be tasked with navigating the team's re-tooled roster on the court.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics will have a re-tooled roster this upcoming season, and question marks surrounding it.

The Celtics added multi-time All-Star wing Paul George, defending NBA champion and center Mitchell Robinson and veteran point guard Mike Conley this offseason, which a clear emphasis on improving the defensive capabilities of the team.

However, there's still a question over how the team will fit on offense.

Former NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers this past offseason in return for George (and draft picks). Robinson will likely split time in the front court with Neemias Queta, who's coming off a career-best season and a contract extension.

And point guard Payton Pritchard will likely play a focal role in getting all the new pieces to fit together on offense.

Pritchard is coming off his sixth season in the NBA and the first as Boston's primary point guard after spending years as the team's sixth man, including winning the Sixth Man of the Year in 2025.

The former Oregon Duck posted his best season as a professional in the 2025-26 season. He averaged 17 points per game on 46.4% shooting from the floor (37.7% from 3-point range) across 79 games (50 starts). He also averaged 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds, both of which were career-highs.

Pritchard's growth as a scorer was important for the team, which was without superstar Jayson Tatum for the majority of the team. But his facilitating took a big jump even without Tatum in the fold.

Pritchard will enter this season as the team's starting point guard and will be backed up by one of the most respected veterans in the Association in Conley. This will allow Pritchard to manage the offense when Tatum doesn't have the ball in his hands. Conley coming off the bench will also allow the Celtics to maintain their defensive pressure when Pritchard isn't on the court.

Being able to make sure Queta continues his impact from his career-best season as the team's starting center while maximizing George and Robinson's impact on the offensive end of the court will be key for Boston to having the best results possible this upcoming season.

Pritchard, as the point guard of the offense, will be tasked as the floor general to make sure that happens.

The Celtics and Pritchard will play their first preseason game against the Cleveland Cavaliers at 7 p.m. ET on Oct. 8 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland.

articles.title: Angel Reese takes a shot at the Chicago Sky after winning WNBA DPOY award
articles.summary: Angel Reese took a dig at her former team, the Chicago Sky, after being named the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year. Angel Reese was named the Defensive...
articles.body:
Angel Reese took a dig at her former team, the Chicago Sky, after being named the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year.

Angel Reese was named the Defensive Player of the Year right before the Atlanta Dream's Game 1 clash in the Semifinals of the WNBA Playoffs. The 24-year-old was handed her trophy and she immediately showed why she deserves it with a dominant display in their 92-82 win.

Reese may be flying with the Dream, but they are not the team which drafted her. Coming in as one of women's basketball's biggest prospects, Reese was drafted by the Chicago Sky with the seventh overall pick in 2024. As she won her first major individual award, she had some words for her former team.

Angel Reese says 'she didn't have the opportunity' to show who she was in the WNBA for the past two years

Despite being named an All-Star in her first two seasons, Reese's time with the Sky was marked with failure. She never made the playoffs with them, and her offensive game was a big target for ridicule within the WNBA world. There were also reports of problems behind the scenes.

For any who may still have been in doubt about how Reese feels regarding her former employers, her words after winning the DPOY are an excellent look into how she feels about them.

"I knew who I was going to be coming into the league. Obviously, I didn't have the opportunity to do that in the past two years," Reese said. "Being able to come here to Atlanta, I knew what I was expected (to do); I knew that I was gonna be put on a pedestal of being able to play with great players… Being able to be here in Atlanta, just really grateful to have sisters in the locker room that genuinely care about me."

The Sky finished this season with a poor 16-28 record once again, missing out on the postseason by a wide margin. Now, their former star is taking shots at them as she succeeds in her very first season with another team. It is a tough time to be a Chicago fan.

articles.title: Atlanta's Ray Kerr got NLDS Game 2 start in the morning. At night, he struck out Shohei Ohtani
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Ray Kerr is becoming an unlikely postseason hero for the Atlanta Braves.The former convenience store and movie theater worker struck out f...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Ray Kerr is becoming an unlikely postseason hero for the Atlanta Braves .

The former convenience store and movie theater worker struck out four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani on a 95-mph four-seam fastball in the Braves' 3-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday night that evened their National League Division Series at a game apiece.

"He did it again for us, just amazing," Braves manager Walt Weiss said. "He's throwing the ball so well."

Ohtani was one of a season-high-tying four strikeouts for Kerr, a 32-year-old lefty reliever who found out in the morning that he'd be starting Game 2 that night. He allowed two hits and walked one in 2 2/3 innings.

"I didn't really have much pressure on me," Kerr said, explaining that he had breakfast with his wife and baby who are on the trip and went swimming. "And then when I got to the field, I developed my process in my head. Just an hour before the game, stretch, and get out there and only throw for like five, six minutes."

Kerr was the opener in the Braves' NL Wild Card Series Game 3 clincher over the Philadelphia Phillies, tossing 3 1/3 scoreless innings, with one hit, one walk and two strikeouts.

"It's been fun. It's very surprising," he said. "It's like one night, all of a sudden, I got a thousand followers on Instagram. I'm getting used to it. I'm just going to be myself throughout it."

At 13, Kerr landed in the foster care system in Reno, Nevada, because his father was in prison and his mother was absent. He and his brother were eventually taken in by a woman who provided the stability that had been lacking in their lives.

Kerr graduated from high school in Reno and played baseball at Mendocino College in Northern California for two years before quitting the sport. He returned home and took jobs at a 7-Eleven and a theater.

A coach at Lassen College in the Sierra Nevada foothills convinced Kerr to join the team. He went on to play in the Alaska Baseball League in 2017, where his fastball touched 93 mph. That August, he signed with the Seattle Mariners as an undrafted free agent.

In 2021, he was traded to the San Diego Padres. The following season he reached the majors for the first time, appearing in seven games before being sent down to Triple-A in 2023. Late that year, he was traded to the Braves and started the 2024 season at Triple-A.

He had Tommy John surgery, ending his season in June and keeping him out all of 2025. He returned this year and got selected to Atlanta's active roster in August.

Kerr made his season debut on Aug. 17, and posted a 1.47 ERA over 18 1/3 innings in nine appearances. Left-handed hitters — like Ohtani — hit .174 against him with a double being the only extra-base hit he allowed.

The Braves are headed back to Atlanta for Game 3 on Tuesday, when ace Chris Sale is expected to start.

"It's going to be crazy there," Kerr said. "The crowd's going to be beautiful to watch. I already know it. Especially against the Dodgers."

And if Kerr gets the nod to take down more innings again, he'll tell himself "All right, let's get it."

"That's what I say every time," he said, "and then I stick to it."

articles.title: Penguins Linked To $92.8 Million Star Forward
articles.summary: The discussion that fans of the Pittsburgh Penguins know is coming at some point is at least a full season away, but they won’t be able to ignore it much lon...
articles.body:
The discussion that fans of the Pittsburgh Penguins know is coming at some point is at least a full season away, but they won't be able to ignore it much longer.

The iconic duo of Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin aren't getting any younger, and both players are going to call it a career sooner rather than later; right now, the prevailing thought is that 2026-27 could be the last year of Malkin's career, while Crosby is also entering the last year of his current contract.

The Penguins are going to need a reliable source of offense from a notable name to help carry the load when both players decide to hang up the skates, and right now, they're being named as having an outside shot to land an intriguing forward.

NHL Insider Links Pittsburgh Penguins To Canucks Forward Elias Pettersson

According to noted Vancouver Canucks insider Rick Dhaliwal, the Penguins have "some degree" of interest in Pettersson, though there's no current traction on any kind of deal.

"I do believe Pittsburgh has some degree of interest in Elias Pettersson. I am not hearing the rumour that the Canucks have asked for Ben Kindel; no way the Penguins are gonna give up such a promising young player… for a bad contract," Dhaliwal said.

"Teams that are desperate at center call; I checked in this morning, Pettersson has not been asked… to waive his no-move; that tells you… there's nothing close," Dhaliwal added.

Pettersson remains with the Canucks for now despite having been heavily involved in trade rumors over the last several months. While Vancouver traded away the likes of Quinn Hughes, Conor Garland, Tyler Myers, and Kiefer Sherwood last season, Pettersson remained in place.

He still has six years, including the current 2026-27 campaign, left on his contract with an $11.6 million salary cap hit.

Could Elias Pettersson Eventually Land With The Penguins?

The Swedish forward continues to be the subject of trade rumors despite carrying multiple years and a hefty salary cap hit on his contract.

Pettersson, whom the Canucks selected in the first round (fifth overall pick) in the 2017 NHL Draft, has skated in 548 career games and has scored 202 goals with 311 assists. He's also contributed eight goals with 16 assists in 30 games in the Stanley Cup Playoffs.

So far this year, he's tallied twice while adding three assists in three games played.

articles.title: Tobias Harris reveals why he already loves playing alongside Victor Wembanyama
articles.summary: Tobias Harris is already loving his time playing for the Spurs.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has cemented his place among the greatest players in the league today. He has already managed to lead the San Antonio Spurs to the NBA Finals, and he is drawing all kinds of players to help him compete for the championship.

The latest big name to join the Spurs in the latest offseason was Tobias Harris. He went from playing for the #1-seeded Detroit Pistons to possibly the most promising team in the NBA, which just made it to its first NBA Finals as a core group.

Tobias Harris loves what he has seen from Victor Wembanyama up close

Harris has seen and played against Wembanyama before, but now that he's up close, he is getting to see what makes him special behind the scenes. Wembanyama has proven to be one of the league's biggest stars both literally and figuratively.

Defensively, Wembanyama can clean up almost anything with his defensive instincts and his natural size. Offensively, Wembanyama has shown that he can be a dominant player, but he also has some room for improvement.

As a veteran who is also quite an accomplished offensive player, Harris can have a huge impact on Wembanyama's development. Moving forward, it seems that this will be a great addition for the Spurs because they know that Harris provides all types of positive strengths on and off the court.

"He's one of the hardest workers that I've seen in this game. He's such a student of the game, an intelligent player, and very responsive to any type of feedback on the game. Very great to be around; I haven't been around him too long, but I'm looking forward to getting out there and going to battle with him," Harris said about Wembanyama during the Spurs' Media Day .

Moving forward, it will be tough to stop the Spurs because they will have an even better team this time around. They have the experience now, and they are motivated to perform. They even got reinforcements with Harris, so it will be an even more dangerous team to play against, especially with a rejuvanated Wembanyama.
